review_notes: Read all 558 lines of the target file and inspected Mathlib's Polynomial.Bivariate (equivMvPolynomial, Bivariate.swap), the project's BivariateResultant, BivariateGauss, AuxiliaryFamily, PlaneCurveDiscriminantBound, PlaneCurveLocalReciprocalDiscriminant, and Markoff/TraceCurve/WeightedIrreducibility. The main issue found is definition-level duplication of the bivariate presentation; theorem-only duplications such as degreeOf_map_eq_of_injective versus Mathlib's degrees_map_of_injective, and the various natDegree lemmas, were excluded under the rubric. I could not run Lean, so the proposed abbrev definition and the resulting simp proofs are untested; the identification is supported by the existing equality theorems and identical definition bodies.

findings.excerpt:
def planeCurveToBivariate (K : Type*) [Field K] :
    MvPolynomial (Fin 2) K ≃ₐ[K] Polynomial (Polynomial K) :=
  (MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv K 1).trans
    (Polynomial.mapAlgEquiv (MvPolynomial.uniqueAlgEquiv K (Fin 1)))
findings.problem: planeCurveToBivariate is a new algebra equivalence with the same type and body as the existing finTwoToIteratedPolynomial in Markoff/TraceCurve/WeightedIrreducibility.lean, and it is the transpose of the existing planeCurvePolynomialInSecondCoordinate in PlaneCurveDiscriminantBound.lean. Both local presentations are just Mathlib's Polynomial.Bivariate.equivMvPolynomial up to .symm and Mathlib's Polynomial.Bivariate.swap: the new transposeBivariate_planeCurveToBivariate and the existing planeCurvePolynomialInSecondCoordinate_eq_bivariateEquiv both identify the transpose of the respective local equivalence with (Polynomial.Bivariate.equivMvPolynomial K).symm. The file then repeats the _X_zero, _X_one, and _C simp API and proves separate degree and evaluation lemmas, so downstream users must transport between same-typed equivalences via transposeBivariate. This is a concrete duplicated API, not merely a different notation.
findings.proposed_change: Keep a single presentation. At minimum make planeCurveToBivariate an abbrev for the existing finTwoToIteratedPolynomial (moving that generic declaration to a shared module), or define it as (Polynomial.Bivariate.equivMvPolynomial K).symm.trans Polynomial.Bivariate.swap; make planeCurvePolynomialInSecondCoordinate the same shared definition (or its transposeBivariate). Derive the _X_zero, _X_one, _C, natDegree, and evaluation lemmas from Mathlib's equivMvPolynomial_symm_X_0, equivMvPolynomial_symm_X_1, equivMvPolynomial_symm_C, Bivariate.swap_X, Bivariate.swap_Y, Bivariate.swap_C_C, and the existing local lemmas instead of copying the proofs. Preserve planeCurveToBivariate as an alias if the name is needed downstream.
findings.benefit: One canonical presentation removes the duplicate AlgEquiv and its copied simp lemmas, eliminates conversions between planeCurveToBivariate, finTwoToIteratedPolynomial, and planeCurvePolynomialInSecondCoordinate, and makes the relation to Mathlib's bivariate API explicit for downstream users.

evidence.excerpt:
def equivMvPolynomial : R[X][Y] ≃ₐ[R] MvPolynomial (Fin 2) R :=
  .ofAlgHom (aevalAeval (.X 0) (.X 1)) (MvPolynomial.aeval ![.C X, X])

def Bivariate.swap : R[X][Y] ≃ₐ[R] R[X][Y] := by
  apply AlgEquiv.ofAlgHom (aevalAeval (Y : R[X][Y]) (C X)) (aevalAeval (Y : R[X][Y]) (C X))

noncomputable def finTwoToIteratedPolynomial :
    MvPolynomial (Fin 2) K ≃ₐ[K] Polynomial K[X] :=
  (MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv K 1).trans
    (Polynomial.mapAlgEquiv (MvPolynomial.uniqueAlgEquiv K (Fin 1)))

def planeCurvePolynomialInSecondCoordinate :
    MvPolynomial (Fin 2) K ≃ₐ[K] Polynomial (Polynomial K) :=
  (MvPolynomial.renameEquiv K (Equiv.swap (0 : Fin 2) 1)).trans
    ((MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv K 1).trans
      (Polynomial.mapAlgEquiv (MvPolynomial.uniqueAlgEquiv K (Fin 1))))
